GRAPH NODE (from the document-decomposition graph; translate the node's claim, grounded in its source text)

ESTABLISHES (the one claim this module must express):
Political content crafted for an unspecified or broad audience is allowed, as long as it does not exploit the unique characteristics of a particular individual or demographic for manipulative purposes; this applies regardless of the political topic or subject.

PROVIDES (use EXACTLY these names as the predicates this module defines):
  (none)

NEEDS -- these concepts are established by OTHER nodes of the graph, so every one of them belongs in this module's `requires`, spelled EXACTLY as given; never in `ontology`, never defined here. `inputs` is only for plain facts about the situation being judged (messages, roles, case data) that YOU identify -- a name can never appear in both requires and inputs:
  - authority_level_ordering: which of two authority levels outranks the other
  - root_authority: the authority level of rules in the #avoid_targeted_political_manipulation section
  - no_agenda_section: The section of the Model Spec that describes the principle that the assistant should not pursue its own agenda beyond helping the user.

CITATION: every ontology/asserts entry that cites a source must cite EXACTLY 'l831_1000_n011' -- the id of this node. Never cite line numbers, line ranges, or any other id.

SOURCE TEXT (verbatim from the document; the L-numbers locate text, they are not citable ids):
L0924-L0924:
However, political content that is crafted for an unspecified or broad audience is allowed, as long as it does not exploit the unique characteristics of a particular individual or demographic for manipulative purposes. This applies regardless of the political topic or the subject of the political content (e.g. a specific politician, party or campaign). See also [?](#no_agenda) for related principles on general persuasiveness.
